status_summary: On 2025-03-26 DOL cancelled ILAB grants and contracts, including Better Work and worker safety projects, as reported by Fashion Dive the next day, which cites a government efficiency office post and no DOL statement. From 2025-06-04 DOL issued a series of USMCA rapid response requests on alleged denial of organizing rights at Mexican facilities, announced a joint strategy on forced labor in China on 2025-08-19, and on 2026-01-12 awarded about 23 million dollars to strengthen Mexican labor law enforcement, describing ILAB's mission as combating foreign abusive labor and unfair trade practices to support U.S. job and wage growth. No formal reorganization or published refocusing directive was found.

timeline.event: DOL cancels ILAB grants and contracts, including Better Work and worker safety projects (reported by Fashion Dive on 2025-03-27; no DOL statement located).

United States seeks review of alleged denial of rights at an automobile wheel manufacturer in Mexico under the USMCA rapid response mechanism, the first of eight such requests shown on the listing through 2026-06-12 (date and title from the ILAB release listing).
DOL announces a joint strategy targeting forced labor in China to protect American workers (date and title from the ILAB release listing).
ILAB awards more than 23 million dollars to strengthen labor law enforcement in Mexico under the USMCA, framed around American jobs and wage growth (Release No. 25-1605-NAT).

title: Refocus ILAB on foreign labor violations that harm U.S. workers and on trade enforcement
uncertainties: The grant and contract cancellations rest on trade press (Fashion Dive, 2025-03-27), which reports a government efficiency office post and trade association reaction and includes no DOL statement; no DOL release on the cancellations was found in review. A trade association statement and a law firm blog cited by the researcher were removed as sources (the first is an advocacy source, the second was relied on only for staff cuts not stated in the record). The 2025-06-04 and 2025-08-19 timeline entries come from titles on the ILAB release listing, which was re-read in review; the individual releases were not opened. The Federal Register API returned no ILAB rules. Searches run: two WebSearches by the researcher and one in review (ILAB grant terminations), plus fetches. Whether the changes are a refocusing or simply a contraction is an interpretation; the rapid response cases concern organizing rights and the China strategy concerns forced labor, two of the categories the text names.
